newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebel team to leave for South Africa talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebel team to leave for South Africa talks.

text.p: A rebel delegation was expected to leave eastern Zaire on Thursday for South Africa for the first negotiations between Zaire's warring sides, rebel officials said.

Gaetan Kakudgi, cooperation commissioner for the rebel Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, told Reuters the team for the talks was expected to leave Goma later on Thursday.

Witnesses said a plane from South Africa arrived on Thursday at Goma to pick up the delegation led by Bizima Karaha, rebel foreign affairs commissioner, who headed a rebel team to an Organisation of African Unity (OAU) summit in Togo last week.
Witnesses said rebel leader Laurent Kabila left Goma by air on Thursday for an undisclosed destination ahead of the talks.
Diplomatic sources said on Wednesday that Kabila had been expected in Zimbabwe to seek the support of President Robert Mugabe and his influence within the OAU before the talks in South Africa.
A diplomatic source said Kabila was also likely to be targeting other southern African leaders for their understanding and possible support of his campaign to oust President Mobutu Sese Seko.
In Cape Town, South African and U.N. officials met in Pretoria on Thursday to wrap up arrangements for the talks.
Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad and joint U.N. and OAU envoy Mohamed Sahnoun discussed arrangements which were likely to be made public on Friday, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said.
